message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's morally acceptable for me to tell my mom not to touch my flute. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, my relationship with my mom isn't great. It's been that way since I moved in with my boyfriend, and even though things have slightly improved, they're still not ideal. I don't have all my stuff at her place because we're planning to move to Henderson in October. Right now, I only have essentials with me. I baby it a lot, and I don't let anyone touch it, not even other experienced flute players. It's currently at my mom's house, and she knows I never want her to touch it, not even if it's in the case. This flute isn't just any old student model; it's an Azumi Atlus, a professional model. My mom likes to say that she helped me get it, and in a way, she did. When I was 17, I couldn't sign a contract at the music store on my own, so she signed for it in her name and set up the payment plan. However, I paid for it myself. Within 10 months (on a 12-month plan), I paid off $2,316. It was my solid silver baby, and I finally owned it. Paying it off early even bumped my mom's credit score. But now, she thinks that since she helped me get it, she can touch it whenever she wants. Today, when she was picking me up, I told her I needed to grab my flute, which is hidden at her house in a safe spot. She said she could just bring it, but I firmly said no. Now, she won't stop calling and texting me, demanding to know where it is and saying, "I got it for you, I can touch it whenever I want." She thinks I'm being disrespectful for not letting her touch my very delicate and expensive instrument. So, is it morally acceptable for me to tell my mom not to touch my flute? Let's break this down. First, ownership. I paid for the flute entirely, even though my mom signed the contract. Legally, since I paid it off, it's mine. She helped facilitate the purchase, but the ownership is mine. Second, respect for personal property. I have the right to decide who touches my belongings, especially something as delicate and expensive as a professional flute. My mom's actions seem to disregard my wishes and ownership. Third, the emotional aspect. My mom and I don't have a great relationship, and this situation might be exacerbating any existing tensions. Her persistence in wanting to touch the flute despite my clear instructions could be seen as intrusive or disrespectful. Fourth, communication. I told her not to touch it, but she's not respecting that boundary. It might be helpful to have a calm conversation about why I feel this way and to set clear boundaries. Fifth, the potential consequences. If she continues to insist on touching the flute, there could be damage to it, which would be a loss for me. It's important to protect my property. Lastly, cultural or familial expectations. In some cultures, parents might expect more control over their children's belongings, but in this case, since I'm an adult and own the flute, that expectation might not apply. Considering all these points, it seems morally acceptable for me to tell my mom not to touch my flute. I have ownership rights, and it's reasonable to protect my personal property. However, improving communication and setting clear boundaries might help prevent future conflicts.
